---
applyTo: "projects/plugins/**/*"
---

# WordPress Plugins Instructions

## Plugin Structure

WordPress plugins in `projects/plugins/` are complete WordPress plugins that can be installed and activated on WordPress sites.

## Key Files

- `{plugin-name}.php` - Main plugin file with plugin header
- `readme.txt` - WordPress.org plugin readme
- `composer.json` - PHP dependencies
- `package.json` - JavaScript dependencies and build scripts
- `CHANGELOG.md` - User-facing changelog (generated)
- `changelog/` - Changelog entry files
- `/src` - Source code (PHP, JS, CSS)
- `/tests` - Test files

## WordPress Compatibility

- Support current WordPress version and immediate previous version
- Declare minimum WordPress version in plugin header and readme.txt
- Test with WordPress' minimum PHP version (usually 7.2+, check readme.txt)
- Graceful degradation for older WordPress versions when possible

## Plugin Development

- Use `jetpack build plugins/{plugin-name} --deps` to build with dependencies
- Use `jetpack watch` for continuous building during development
- Activate plugin in Docker environment for testing: http://localhost/wp-admin/
- Test with Docker: `jetpack docker up -d` and `jetpack docker install`

## Plugin Header

Required fields in main plugin file:
```php
/**
 * Plugin Name: Plugin Name
 * Plugin URI: https://jetpack.com/
 * Description: Plugin description
 * Version: 1.0.0
 * Author: Automattic
 * Author URI: https://automattic.com/
 * License: GPL-2.0-or-later
 * Text Domain: plugin-slug
 * Requires at least: 6.5
 * Requires PHP: 7.2
 */
```

## Code Organization

- Separate concerns: PHP business logic, JS for UI, CSS for styles
- Use WordPress hooks (actions/filters) for extensibility
- Namespace PHP code: `Automattic\Jetpack\{PluginName}`
- Use appropriate WordPress APIs (WP_REST_API, Settings API, etc.)
- Register all hooks in main plugin file or bootstrap

## Security

- Sanitize all inputs using WordPress functions (`sanitize_text_field`, etc.)
- Escape all outputs (`esc_html`, `esc_attr`, `esc_url`, etc.)
- Use nonces for all forms and AJAX requests
- Check capabilities before privileged operations
- Validate and sanitize AJAX handlers
- Never trust user input

## Translations

- PHP: Use safe i18n functions (`esc_html__`, `esc_html_e`, `esc_html_x`)
- JavaScript: Use `@wordpress/i18n` with matching text domain
- Text domain should match plugin slug
- Use `automattic/jetpack-composer-plugin` for PHP i18n
- Use `@automattic/babel-plugin-replace-textdomain` for JS i18n

## Testing

- Write PHPUnit tests for PHP code
- Write Jest tests for JavaScript code
- Write Playwright E2E tests for critical user flows
- Run PHP tests: `jetpack test` → select plugin → PHP unit tests
- Run JS tests: `jetpack test` → select plugin → JS tests
- Run in Docker for integration testing

## Database

- Use WordPress database APIs (`$wpdb`, options API, etc.)
- Create/update tables in activation hook or upgrade routine
- Prefix custom tables with `$wpdb->prefix`
- Document schema changes in upgrade routines
- Clean up data in uninstall.php, not deactivation hook

## Asset Loading

- Enqueue scripts/styles properly (`wp_enqueue_script`, `wp_enqueue_style`)
- Use webpack for bundling (shared config in `js-packages/webpack-config`)
- Use asset dependency files generated by webpack
- Localize scripts with `wp_localize_script` for passing data to JS
- Load admin assets only on admin pages
- Load frontend assets only when needed

## WordPress.com Integration

- Some plugins require Jetpack connection to WordPress.com
- Test connection features with Jurassic Tube (Automatticians) or ngrok
- Document connection requirements in readme
